correctness.rationale: At r_*=X+log(1−h/X), X(X−h)=h, define b=X−h=h/X and a=1−b. The (N+1)-dimensional linearization has polynomial λ^(N+1)−aλ^N+b. At a root b=|λ|^N|λ−a|, ruling out |λ|≥1 by the reverse triangle inequality, including equality λ=1 which is not a root. For near-unit branches set λ=exp(z/N) and solve exp(z)(exp(z/N)−a)=−b around odd multiples of iπ. The IFT expansion gives log|λ|=−a(2m+1)²π²/(2b²N³)+O(N^-4) and phase π/N−π/(bN²)+O(N^-3). Every maximal-modulus root has bounded z=Nlogλ and must lie on finitely many such branches; |2m+1|=1 gives exactly one dominant conjugate pair and 1−ρ_N=aπ²/(2b²N³)+O(N^-4). Independently solved dominant branch numerically for h=1 at N=30,100,400; scaled gap approaches π²/2; finite tests not universal proof.
